title: What {name} is: an AI assistant in a browser tab, in plain words
description: {name} is an AI assistant in a browser tab: one box, the AI you choose, files in and out, and your work kept on this device. Nothing to install.
works: Every browser, on a computer or a phone
answer: {name} is an AI assistant in a browser tab. You write, dictate or drop a file in its box, and it answers: words, tables, charts, documents, slides. Nothing to install, no account at {name}, and your work stays on this device.
parts: Everything starts in the box: a question, a task, a file, a folder, a picture. Each request and what came of it make a task, kept in the list of tasks.
{name} works with the AI you choose, which it calls a brain: a free account, a plan or a key you already have, or a brain on this computer. You can change it any time. See {choose}.
It works things out, then makes them
For figures, {name} writes a small program and runs it in a sandbox in the browser, so they are calculated, not guessed. It makes Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, and opens them beside the task.

Your tasks and files are kept in this browser, on this device, encrypted. There is no {name} server: a brain in the cloud reads only what a request sends it, and a brain on this computer sends nothing at all.
Before it sends, shares, deletes or uses the internet, {name} asks you. Passwords and payments: never. See {asks}.
More shows up as you go

{name} starts simple. When a moment calls for more, a spreadsheet dropped in for instance, it offers what helps, one thing at a time. {settings} › {capabilities} lists everything it can do, and how each one comes.
good: {name} is free and open source. The brain behind it may cost money; OpenRouter’s free account and a brain on this computer don’t.
It speaks 46 languages, and answers in the language you write in.
Once opened, it works without the internet, except for a brain in the cloud, the web and the services you connect.
In Chrome or Edge, it installs as an app with a window of its own; on a phone, it goes on the home screen.
Under the box, it says {mistakes}. Figures are calculated; check the words, as you would a colleague’s.
fixes: It needs a brain first. See {choose}.
A private window keeps nothing once it is closed, and clearing this site’s data deletes everything. A backup keeps a copy: see {backup}.
ask: What can you do for me?
